stem:
Lila looks at the diagram. Line $m$ is given, point $P$ is off $m$, and transversal $t$ cuts $m$ at $E$. The marked angle $\alpha$ at $E$ is copied at $P$ so that new line $n$ through $P$ makes the corresponding angle $\alpha$ with $t$.

Which claim correctly states what that construction produces?

options.text: Copy an angle at $P$ with no transversal that cuts line $m$, and claim the new line is parallel to $m$.
Say that the finished parallel line is what creates transversal $t$ through $m$.
Line $n$ through $P$ is parallel to $m$, because the corresponding angle $\alpha$ was copied from transversal $t$.
Slide a set-square along $m$ and treat that tool method as this corresponding-angle copy.

teacher.key_rationale: Copying the corresponding angle from a transversal that cuts m makes n through P parallel to m. Skipping the cutting transversal, reversing parallel and transversal, or swapping in a set-square slide leave this hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as line m, point P, transversal t, copied corresponding angle alpha, and dashed parallel n.
